sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File purpose and imports
sections.what: Describes a helper that gives step-by-step reasons for modelling choices, with full logging. The shown part only imports libraries and sets up logging; the reasoning functions are not in this packet.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the description at the top of the file.
sections.watch_out: Because the rest of the file is not visible, what it actually does cannot be confirmed.

sections.name: ReasoningAgent (part 1)
sections.title: Reasoning agent setup and model analysis
sections.what: Creates the reasoning agent with low randomness and runs the full analysis through `analyze_model_inputs`. It sends the company, industry and model inputs to the AI and asks for reasoning steps, findings, recommendations, warnings and a confidence score.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed instruction asks the AI for one JSON layout so the app can read every answer the same way.
sections.watch_out: If the AI reply is not valid JSON, the fallback result looks like a normal answer, so the warning text must be checked.

sections.name: ReasoningAgent (part 2)
sections.title: Parsing analysis and starting benchmark comparison
sections.what: Reads the analysis reply as JSON and adds the agent name, a copy of the step log, the model used and the time taken. It then builds the prompt for `compare_to_benchmarks`, which asks how the company's metrics compare with its industry.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code for the parsing fallback beyond keeping the app from crashing on a bad reply.
sections.watch_out: Benchmark comparison relies on the research data passed in; without it, the AI uses only its own memory of industry averages.

sections.name: ReasoningAgent (part 3)
sections.title: Benchmark result and calculation explanation
sections.what: Finishes the benchmark comparison, returning the AI reply as JSON or wrapping raw text if parsing fails. `explain_calculation` then asks the AI to explain a named calculation in plain terms, including inputs, result and typical range.
sections.why: Likely reason: the explanation is meant for a non-expert reader, so the prompt asks for plain language.
sections.watch_out: Both bare except clauses catch every error, not only bad JSON, which can hide real bugs.

sections.name: ReasoningAgent (part 4)
sections.title: Explanation return and scenario suggestions
sections.what: Returns the calculation explanation with its log. `suggest_scenario_analysis` asks the AI for bull and bear case assumptions with reasons, probability estimates and key drivers, and returns them as JSON or as raw text.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code for why scenarios are AI guesses rather than rule-based.
sections.watch_out: The probabilities and adjusted values come from the AI and are not checked against any rule, so they need human review before use.

sections.name: ReasoningAgent: _build_analysis_prompt
sections.title: Building the analysis prompt
sections.what: Assembles the text sent to the AI: the model inputs, any research data, and a fixed checklist covering revenue growth, margins, capital spending and working capital, valuation inputs, and red flags.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed checklist makes every analysis cover the same areas.
sections.watch_out: The whole inputs dictionary is pasted in as text, so a very large model can make the prompt too long for the AI.
